title: Authentication & Session Design: Cookies, Tokens & Refresh Rotation
concept: Design login sessions that survive real attacks and real traffic: server sessions versus tokens, cookie flags, short-lived access tokens, refresh tokens stored as hashes, revocation, rotation with token families, replay detection and concurrent refresh, each taught from a security incident and graded with small TypeScript programs.
description: An advanced course for backend developers who own the login of a production app. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a session cookie that any injected script can read, an access token that is still accepted a day after logout, a database backup that leaked every refresh token in plain text, a stolen refresh token that keeps working after the learner signs in again, two browser tabs that refresh at the same moment and log the learner out - and fixes it with sound session design: choosing between server sessions and tokens, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite and Path, CSRF and XSS exposure, signed access tokens with expiry checked against a clock, refresh tokens stored only as hashes, logout from one device or all of them, refresh token rotation by family, replay detection that revokes the whole family, and compare-and-swap rotation under concurrent requests. The code runs on deterministic fakes - a fake clock, an in-memory session store, fixed keys - so every attack can be replayed in a test. 10 lessons with quizzes on real headers, logs and code and hands-on TypeScript challenges.

lessons.title: Choose a session model: server sessions or tokens
Set session cookies right: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite & Path
CSRF, XSS and the token cookie an AI made readable
Short-lived access tokens: sign, verify and expire
Store refresh tokens as hashes, never as secrets
Revoke sessions: log out one device or all of them
Detect refresh token replay and revoke the family
Concurrent refresh: two tabs, one token, compare-and-swap
Incident: refresh tokens leaked in plain text
